okerror.py.summary: Sort the Python files of the current directory into ``ok`` and ``error`` folders with ``black --check``.
details: Runs ``black --check`` on every top-level ``.py`` file (the running script excluded), moves the files that already match black into ``ok/`` and the rest into ``error/``, renaming on collision.
okerror.py.notes: Moves every ``.py`` file out of the current directory; run it in a scratch folder.

details: Loads each ``.otf`` file with fontTools, sets the ``woff2`` flavour and saves ``<name>.woff2`` next to it (a unique name when that file already exists). Files named on the command line or found below the current directory are converted in parallel.

outcast.py.summary: Copy the largest file of the Telegram cache to ``/sdcard/Download`` as an ``.mkv``.
details: Scans ``/sdcard/Android/data/org.telegram.messenger/cache`` for the biggest file, copies it to the download folder under a random six-letter name and prints its size in megabytes.
outcast.py.notes: The source and destination paths are fixed in the module (Termux/Android layout).

pathcmd.py.summary: Print every directory on ``PATH``, one per line.
details: Splits ``$PATH`` on colons and prints the entries in order, which makes it easy to spot duplicates or stale directories.

pathdiag.py.summary: Diagnose the shell setup: ``PATH`` entries, executables, aliases and functions.
details: Lists the entries of ``PATH`` with duplicate detection, hashes the executables it finds, and extracts the aliases and functions defined by the shell rc file (``~/.bashrc`` by default). ``--fix-dedup`` rewrites the rc file without the repeated entries.

pdf2img.py.summary: Render the PDFs below the current directory to JPEG pages.
details: Converts each page at 300 dpi into ``output_jpgs/<name>/<name>_page_N.jpg`` with PyMuPDF and deletes the original PDF after a successful conversion; failed conversions keep their sources and are counted in the summary.
pdf2img.py.notes: Deletes each PDF once all of its pages were written.

pdf2png.py.summary: Render a PDF to PNG files with ``pdftoppm``.
details: Calls poppler's ``pdftoppm`` for the given file at the requested dpi (200 by default), writes the images into the output directory (named after the PDF when omitted) and renumbers them as ``<name>_page_NNN.png``.

pdftotext.py.summary: Extract the text of PDF files with a choice of backends.
details: ``--backend`` selects fitz (PyMuPDF), pypdf, pdfplumber or pdfminer; pages can be joined or written one file per page with ``--perpage``, spaces are normalised, and ``--password`` opens protected documents.

pdif.py.summary: Compare two text files and report the differing line numbers.
details: Prints the line count of both files, how many lines they share and the one-based numbers of the lines that only occur in one of them.

pdiff.py.summary: Compare two Python files at the AST, bytecode or disassembly level.
details: Modes select the comparison: ``ast`` dumps both syntax trees, ``dis`` shows the disassembly and the default diffs the compiled bytecode opcodes, so files that differ only in formatting or comments compare equal.

perpage.py.summary: Split PDFs into one file per page or extract the text page by page.
details: Processes the PDFs given on the command line (or found below the current directory) with pypdf in a worker pool. ``--text`` writes ``.txt`` files per page instead of single-page PDFs, and ``--output-dir`` selects where the results go (``./output`` by default).

pfzf.py.summary: A dependency-free fuzzy finder with an interactive prompt.
details: Scores and ranks the lines read from stdin (or a built-in demo list) while you type, rendering the matches with the matched characters highlighted; arrow keys move the selection and Enter prints it. ``--filter QUERY`` prints the ranked matches non-interactively.

pip_sanity_check.py.summary: Check that every installed distribution can still be imported.
details: Imports each package reported by ``importlib.metadata.distributions()`` and prints the failures (with the exception) plus a summary of how many packages import cleanly.

piu.py.summary: Uninstall pip packages by name or by substring.
details: Matches the arguments against the installed distribution names and calls ``pip uninstall -y`` for the matches. ``-w`` treats the arguments as substrings instead of exact names.
